in.title: Kembali Mundur: Mengapa Perdebatan Waktu Musim Panas Permanen Terus Mandek

segments.src: Every autumn, Americans gain an hour of sleep and lose an hour of evening light.
segments.tr: Setiap musim gugur, warga Amerika mendapatkan tambahan satu jam tidur dan kehilangan satu jam cahaya malam hari.

segments.src: With clocks having just turned back for the year, a familiar question returns: why are we still doing this twice a year?
segments.tr: Dengan jam yang baru saja dimundurkan untuk tahun ini, pertanyaan yang familier kembali muncul: mengapa kita masih melakukan ini dua kali setahun?

segments.src: Polls regularly show that many Americans would like to stop changing the clocks.
segments.tr: Jajak pendapat secara berkala menunjukkan bahwa banyak warga Amerika ingin menghentikan pengubahan jam.

segments.src: Yet years of bills, hearings and statehouse debates have produced no national change.
segments.tr: Namun, bertahun-tahun rancangan undang-undang, dengar pendapat, dan perdebatan gedung legislatif negara bagian belum menghasilkan perubahan nasional.

segments.src: The reason has less to do with indifference than with a disagreement over which time to keep.
segments.tr: Alasannya lebih berkaitan dengan ketidaksepakatan tentang waktu mana yang harus dipertahankan daripada ketidakpedulian.

segments.src: ## Where the Law Stands
segments.tr: ## Posisi Hukum Saat Ini

segments.src: Under the Uniform Time Act of 1966, states may opt out of daylight saving time and stay on standard time all year.
segments.tr: Berdasarkan Uniform Time Act tahun 1966, negara bagian dapat memilih untuk tidak mengikuti waktu musim panas dan tetap menggunakan waktu standar sepanjang tahun.

segments.src: Arizona (apart from the Navajo Nation) and Hawaii have done so.
segments.tr: Arizona (terkecuali Suku Navajo) dan Hawaii telah melakukannya.

segments.src: States cannot, however, adopt permanent daylight saving time on their own.
segments.tr: Namun, negara bagian tidak dapat mengadopsi waktu musim panas permanen atas inisiatif mereka sendiri.

segments.src: That change requires an act of Congress.
segments.tr: Perubahan tersebut memerlukan undang-undang dari Kongres.

segments.src: Dozens of states have passed laws or resolutions that would move to year-round daylight time if Congress allowed it.
segments.tr: Puluhan negara bagian telah mengesahkan undang-undang atau resolusi yang akan beralih ke waktu musim panas sepanjang tahun jika Kongres mengizinkannya.

segments.src: These measures are often called "trigger" laws because they take effect only after federal permission.
segments.tr: Langkah-langkah ini sering disebut undang-undang "pemicu" karena baru berlaku setelah ada izin federal.

segments.src: This leaves a patchwork of intentions with no clear path forward.
segments.tr: Hal ini menyisakan tambal sulam niat tanpa arah ke depan yang jelas.

segments.src: ## The Bill That Almost Was
segments.tr: ## Undang-Undang yang Nyaris Terwujud

segments.src: The best-known attempt was the Sunshine Protection Act.
segments.tr: Upaya paling terkenal adalah Sunshine Protection Act.

segments.src: In March 2022 the Senate passed it by unanimous consent, with little debate.
segments.tr: Pada Maret 2022, Senat meloloskannya melalui persetujuan bulat, dengan sedikit perdebatan.

segments.src: The bill would have made daylight saving time permanent nationwide.
segments.tr: Rancangan undang-undang tersebut akan menjadikan waktu musim panas bersifat permanen di seluruh negeri.

segments.src: The House did not take it up, and the bill expired at the end of that session.
segments.tr: DPR tidak membahasnya, dan rancangan undang-undang tersebut kedaluwarsa pada akhir masa sidang itu.

segments.src: Versions have been reintroduced in later Congresses with bipartisan sponsors, and they have again stalled in committee.
segments.tr: Versi-versinya telah diajukan kembali di Kongres berikutnya dengan sponsor bipartisan, dan sekali lagi mengalami kebuntuan di komite.

segments.src: The 2022 episode is often cited as proof of how popular the idea is.
segments.tr: Peristiwa tahun 2022 sering dikutip sebagai bukti betapa populernya gagasan tersebut.

segments.src: It also showed how little consensus lay beneath the surface.
segments.tr: Peristiwa itu juga menunjukkan betapa minimnya konsensus di balik permukaan.

segments.src: Several senators later said they had not examined the details, and some critics argued the chamber had acted without a serious look at the evidence.
segments.tr: Beberapa senator kemudian mengatakan bahwa mereka belum memeriksa detailnya, dan beberapa kritikus berpendapat majelis tersebut bertindak tanpa kajian bukti yang serius.

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Daylight Time
segments.tr: ## Argumen untuk Waktu Musim Panas Permanen

segments.src: Supporters of year-round daylight time point to several benefits:
segments.tr: Pendukung waktu musim panas sepanjang tahun menunjukkan beberapa manfaat:

segments.src: - **Evening light.** Later sunsets year-round mean more daylight after work and school, which supporters say encourages outdoor activity, shopping and recreation.
segments.tr: - **Cahaya malam hari.** Matahari terbenam yang lebih lambat sepanjang tahun berarti lebih banyak cahaya siang hari setelah jam kerja dan sekolah, yang menurut para pendukung mendorong aktivitas luar ruangan, belanja, dan rekreasi.

segments.src: - **Safety.** Some studies suggest that more evening light can reduce certain crimes and may lower the risk of pedestrian crashes during the evening commute, when traffic is heavy.
segments.tr: - **Keamanan.** Beberapa penelitian menunjukkan bahwa lebih banyak cahaya di malam hari dapat mengurangi kejahatan tertentu dan dapat menurunkan risiko kecelakaan pejalan kaki selama jam sibuk malam hari, saat lalu lintas padat.

segments.src: - **Economic activity.** Retail, restaurant and tourism groups have long backed extra daylight hours, arguing that consumers spend more when it is light out.
segments.tr: - **Aktivitas ekonomi.** Kelompok ritel, restoran, dan pariwisata telah lama mendukung tambahan jam siang hari, dengan alasan bahwa konsumen menghabiskan lebih banyak uang saat hari masih terang.

segments.src: - **No more switching.** Ending the twice-yearly change removes the disruption it causes, including a short-term rise in some health and safety problems around the spring shift.
segments.tr: - **Tidak ada lagi pergantian jam.** Mengakhiri perubahan dua kali setahun menghilangkan gangguan yang ditimbulkannya, termasuk peningkatan jangka pendek dalam beberapa masalah kesehatan dan keselamatan di sekitar pergeseran musim semi.

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Standard Time
segments.tr: ## Argumen untuk Waktu Standar Permanen

segments.src: Many sleep scientists and medical groups favor the opposite approach.
segments.tr: Banyak ilmuwan tidur dan kelompok medis menyukai pendekatan sebaliknya.

segments.src: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine and other professional bodies have said that permanent standard time better matches the human body clock, because it aligns more closely with the natural cycle of sunrise and sunset.
segments.tr: American Academy of Sleep Medicine dan badan profesional lainnya menyatakan bahwa waktu standar permanen lebih sesuai dengan jam biologis tubuh manusia, karena lebih sejalan dengan siklus alami terbit dan terbenamnya matahari.

segments.src: Their main points are:
segments.tr: Poin utama mereka adalah:

segments.src: - **Circadian health.** Standard time puts more light in the morning, which helps regulate sleep and alertness. Permanent daylight time would mean very late sunrises in winter, especially in the western parts of time zones. In some places the sun would not rise until well after 8 a.m.
segments.tr: - **Kesehatan sirkadian.** Waktu standar memberikan lebih banyak cahaya di pagi hari, yang membantu mengatur tidur dan kewaspadaan. Waktu musim panas permanen berarti matahari terbit sangat lambat di musim dingin, terutama di bagian barat zona waktu. Di beberapa tempat, matahari bahkan baru akan terbit jauh setelah pukul 08.00.

segments.src: - **Sleep and long-term health.** Researchers have linked chronic misalignment between social clocks and the body clock with sleep loss and other health problems. Advocates say standard time is the safer bet.
segments.tr: - **Tidur dan kesehatan jangka panjang.** Para peneliti telah mengaitkan ketidakselarasan kronis antara jam sosial dan jam tubuh dengan kurang tidur serta masalah kesehatan lainnya. Para advokat mengatakan waktu standar adalah pilihan yang lebih aman.

segments.src: - **School mornings.** Children would commonly wait for buses and walk to school in the dark during winter months under permanent daylight time.
segments.tr: - **Pagi hari sekolah.** Anak-anak biasanya harus menunggu bus dan berjalan ke sekolah dalam gelap selama bulan-bulan musim dingin di bawah waktu musim panas permanen.

segments.src: Evidence on both sides is real but imperfect.
segments.tr: Bukti di kedua sisi bersifat nyata namun tidak sempurna.

segments.src: Studies vary in method and in geography, and a benefit in one region can be a cost in another.
segments.tr: Studi bervariasi dalam metode dan geografi, dan keuntungan di satu wilayah bisa menjadi kerugian di wilayah lain.

segments.src: ## Lessons From the Past
segments.tr: ## Pelajaran dari Masa Lalu

segments.src: The United States has tried this before.
segments.tr: Amerika Serikat pernah mencoba hal ini sebelumnya.

segments.src: In 1974, Congress enacted year-round daylight time as a response to the energy crisis.
segments.tr: Pada tahun 1974, Kongres memberlakukan waktu musim panas sepanjang tahun sebagai respons terhadap krisis energi.

segments.src: Early public support faded within months as winter mornings stayed dark, and Congress reversed course the following year.
segments.tr: Dukungan publik awal memudar dalam beberapa bulan karena pagi hari di musim dingin tetap gelap, dan Kongres membalikkan keputusan tersebut pada tahun berikutnya.

segments.src: Supporters of permanence say today's circumstances are different.
segments.tr: Pendukung kepermanenan mengatakan keadaan saat ini berbeda.

segments.src: Critics say the episode is a warning.
segments.tr: Para kritikus mengatakan episode tersebut adalah sebuah peringatan.

segments.src: ## Why Nothing Gets Done
segments.tr: ## Mengapa Tidak Ada yang Terwujud

segments.src: If both parties like the idea of ending clock changes, why is there no law?
segments.tr: Jika kedua partai menyukai gagasan mengakhiri perubahan jam, mengapa tidak ada undang-undang?

segments.src: Several obstacles stand in the way.
segments.tr: Beberapa hambatan menghalangi jalan.

segments.src: 1. **A split over which time.** Ending the switch is popular, but people who want permanent daylight time and people who want permanent standard time often oppose each other more than they oppose the status quo. A bill that satisfies one camp can lose the other.
segments.tr: 1. **Perpecahan mengenai waktu mana yang dipilih.** Mengakhiri pergantian jam sangat populer, tetapi orang yang menginginkan waktu musim panas permanen dan orang yang menginginkan waktu standar permanen sering kali lebih saling menentang daripada menentang status quo. RUU yang memuaskan satu kubu dapat mengecewakan kubu lainnya.

segments.src: 2. **Regional differences.** A sunrise at 8:30 a.m. is a minor matter in one part of a time zone and a serious one in another. Lawmakers from northern and western areas of a zone often have different priorities from those in the east.
segments.tr: 2. **Perbedaan regional.** Matahari terbit pukul 08.30 adalah masalah sepele di satu bagian zona waktu dan masalah serius di bagian lain. Pembuat undang-undang dari wilayah utara dan barat zona sering kali memiliki prioritas yang berbeda dari mereka yang di timur.

segments.src: 3. **Competing priorities.** Time policy rarely ranks above budgets, security and health care on a crowded legislative calendar. Committee leaders may see it as a low-urgency item with high potential for backlash.
segments.tr: 3. **Prioritas yang bersaing.** Kebijakan waktu jarang sekali berada di atas anggaran, keamanan, dan perawatan kesehatan dalam kalender legislatif yang padat. Pemimpin komite mungkin melihatnya sebagai item prioritas rendah dengan potensi reaksi keras yang tinggi.

segments.src: 4. **Industry and regional concerns.** Transportation, broadcasting, agriculture and finance all depend on time standards. Some businesses worry about misalignment with neighboring states or trading partners if states choose different paths.
segments.tr: 4. **Kepentingan industri dan regional.** Transportasi, penyiaran, pertanian, dan keuangan semuanya bergantung pada standar waktu. Beberapa bisnis khawatir tentang ketidakselarasan dengan negara bagian tetangga atau mitra dagang jika negara bagian memilih jalur yang berbeda.

segments.src: 5. **Fear of repeating 1974.** Lawmakers remember that a popular change was reversed once voters felt the effects.
segments.tr: 5. **Ketakutan mengulangi tahun 1974.** Pembuat undang-undang ingat bahwa perubahan populer pernah dibatalkan begitu pemilih merasakan dampaknya.

segments.src: ## The Statehouse Picture
segments.tr: ## Gambaran Gedung Legislatif Negara Bagian

segments.src: States keep acting even though they cannot finish the job.
segments.tr: Negara-negara bagian terus bertindak meskipun mereka tidak dapat menyelesaikan tugasnya.

segments.src: Some legislatures have passed daylight-time trigger laws.
segments.tr: Beberapa badan legislatif telah mengesahkan undang-undang pemicu waktu musim panas.

segments.src: Others have considered bills for permanent standard time, which they are already allowed to adopt.
segments.tr: Yang lain telah mempertimbangkan RUU untuk waktu standar permanen, yang sudah diizinkan untuk mereka adopsi.

segments.src: A few have proposed regional compacts so that neighboring states move together.
segments.tr: Beberapa telah mengusulkan pakta regional agar negara bagian tetangga bergerak bersama.

segments.src: Each approach has trade-offs, and none solves the national question alone.
segments.tr: Setiap pendekatan memiliki pertukaran, dan tidak ada yang menyelesaikan pertanyaan nasional secara sendirian.

segments.src: ## What Could Break the Logjam
segments.tr: ## Apa yang Dapat Memecah Kebuntuan

segments.src: Possible paths include:
segments.tr: Kemungkinan jalan keluarnya meliputi:

segments.src: - **A compromise bill** that lets each state choose between permanent standard and permanent daylight time, with rules to limit confusion at borders.
segments.tr: - **RUU kompromi** yang memungkinkan setiap negara bagian memilih antara waktu standar permanen dan waktu musim panas permanen, dengan aturan untuk membatasi kebingungan di perbatasan.

segments.src: - **A federal study** that gathers current evidence on health, safety and economic effects before Congress commits.
segments.tr: - **Studi federal** yang mengumpulkan bukti saat ini tentang kesehatan, keselamatan, dan efek ekonomi sebelum Kongres berkomitmen.

segments.src: - **Movement on standard time first**, since states can already adopt it without federal approval, which could build experience and data.
segments.tr: - **Pergerakan pada waktu standar terlebih dahulu**, karena negara bagian sudah dapat mengadopsinya tanpa persetujuan federal, yang dapat membangun pengalaman dan data.

segments.src: Any of these would require sustained attention from leaders who have so far treated the issue as a seasonal curiosity.
segments.tr: Semua ini akan membutuhkan perhatian berkelanjutan dari para pemimpin yang sejauh ini memperlakukan masalah ini sebagai rasa Ingin tahu musiman.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Kesimpulan

segments.src: The clock-change debate persists because it combines wide public frustration with a real scientific and political disagreement.
segments.tr: Perdebatan tentang perubahan jam terus berlanjut karena menggabungkan frustrasi publik yang luas dengan ketidaksepakatan ilmiah dan politik yang nyata.

segments.src: Ending the switch is easy to endorse.
segments.tr: Mengakhiri pergantian jam sangat mudah didukung.

segments.src: Deciding which permanent time to choose, and who bears the cost of dark mornings or early sunsets, is much harder.
segments.tr: Menentukan waktu permanen mana yang harus dipilih, dan siapa yang menanggung biaya pagi hari yang gelap atau matahari terbenam lebih awal, jauh lebih sulit.

segments.src: Until lawmakers settle that question, Americans can expect to keep adjusting their clocks twice a year, and to have this argument again each spring and fall.
segments.tr: Sampai pembuat undang-undang menyelesaikan pertanyaan itu, warga Amerika dapat memperkirakan untuk terus menyesuaikan jam mereka dua kali setahun, dan menghadapi perdebatan ini lagi setiap musim semi dan musim gugur.

ja.title: 再びの「時計の巻き戻し」：なぜ恒久的なサマータイム導入の議論は進まないのか

segments.src: Every autumn, Americans gain an hour of sleep and lose an hour of evening light.
segments.tr: 毎年秋になると、アメリカ人は睡眠時間を1時間得て、夕方の明るい時間を1時間失います。

segments.src: With clocks having just turned back for the year, a familiar question returns: why are we still doing this twice a year?
segments.tr: 今年も時計の針が戻されたことで、おなじみの疑問が再び浮上しています。なぜ私たちは年に2回もこんなことを続けているのでしょうか？

segments.src: Polls regularly show that many Americans would like to stop changing the clocks.
segments.tr: 世論調査では、多くのアメリカ人が時計の変更をやめたいと望んでいることが定期的に示されています。

segments.src: Yet years of bills, hearings and statehouse debates have produced no national change.
segments.tr: しかし、長年にわたる法案提出や公聴会、州議会での議論を経ても、国レベルでの変更は実現していません。

segments.src: The reason has less to do with indifference than with a disagreement over which time to keep.
segments.tr: その理由は、無関心というよりは、どちらの時間を維持すべきかという意見の不一致にあります。

segments.src: ## Where the Law Stands
segments.tr: ## 現行法の状況

segments.src: Under the Uniform Time Act of 1966, states may opt out of daylight saving time and stay on standard time all year.
segments.tr: 1966年の統一時間法（Uniform Time Act）に基づき、各州はサマータイム（夏時間）の適用を除外し、年間を通じて標準時を採用することができます。

segments.src: Arizona (apart from the Navajo Nation) and Hawaii have done so.
segments.tr: アリゾナ州（ナバホ・ネイションを除く）とハワイ州はすでにこれを行っています。

segments.src: States cannot, however, adopt permanent daylight saving time on their own.
segments.tr: しかし、州が独自に恒久的なサマータイムを採用することはできません。

segments.src: That change requires an act of Congress.
segments.tr: その変更には連邦議会の法案が必要です。

segments.src: Dozens of states have passed laws or resolutions that would move to year-round daylight time if Congress allowed it.
segments.tr: 数十の州が、連邦議会が許可すれば通年でサマータイムに移行するという法律や決議を可決しています。

segments.src: These measures are often called "trigger" laws because they take effect only after federal permission.
segments.tr: これらの措置は、連邦政府の許可があって初めて発効するため、しばしば「トリガー（引き金）」法と呼ばれます。

segments.src: This leaves a patchwork of intentions with no clear path forward.
segments.tr: このため、明確な前進の道筋がないまま、意図だけがちぐはぐな状態で残されています。

segments.src: ## The Bill That Almost Was
segments.tr: ## 実現しかけた法案

segments.src: The best-known attempt was the Sunshine Protection Act.
segments.tr: 最もよく知られた試みは「サンシャイン保護法（Sunshine Protection Act）」でした。

segments.src: In March 2022 the Senate passed it by unanimous consent, with little debate.
segments.tr: 2022年3月、上院はほとんど議論することなく、全会一致でこの法案を可決しました。

segments.src: The bill would have made daylight saving time permanent nationwide.
segments.tr: この法案は、サマータイムを全国で恒久化するものでした。

segments.src: The House did not take it up, and the bill expired at the end of that session.
segments.tr: 下院では審議されず、法案はその会期の終了とともに失効しました。

segments.src: Versions have been reintroduced in later Congresses with bipartisan sponsors, and they have again stalled in committee.
segments.tr: その後の議会でも超党派の提案者によって修正案が再提出されていますが、いずれも委員会で停滞しています。

segments.src: The 2022 episode is often cited as proof of how popular the idea is.
segments.tr: 2022年の出来事は、このアイデアがいかに人気があるかを証明するものとしてよく引用されます。

segments.src: It also showed how little consensus lay beneath the surface.
segments.tr: また、その裏側にいかに合意が欠けていたかも示しました。

segments.src: Several senators later said they had not examined the details, and some critics argued the chamber had acted without a serious look at the evidence.
segments.tr: 後に数人の上院議員が詳細を検討していなかったと述べ、一部の批判者は、議会が証拠を真剣に検討することなく行動したと主張しました。

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Daylight Time
segments.tr: ## 恒久的なサマータイムを支持する論拠

segments.src: Supporters of year-round daylight time point to several benefits:
segments.tr: 通年サマータイムの支持者は、いくつかの利点を挙げています。

segments.src: - **Evening light.** Later sunsets year-round mean more daylight after work and school, which supporters say encourages outdoor activity, shopping and recreation.
segments.tr: - **夕方の明るさ。** 一年を通して日没が遅くなることで、仕事や学校の後に明るい時間が増え、屋外活動や買い物、レクリエーションが促進されると支持者は主張しています。

segments.src: - **Safety.** Some studies suggest that more evening light can reduce certain crimes and may lower the risk of pedestrian crashes during the evening commute, when traffic is heavy.
segments.tr: - **安全性。** いくつかの研究では、夕方の明るい時間が増えることで特定の犯罪が減少し、交通量の多い夕方の通勤時間帯における歩行者の衝突事故リスクが低下する可能性があることが示唆されています。

segments.src: - **Economic activity.** Retail, restaurant and tourism groups have long backed extra daylight hours, arguing that consumers spend more when it is light out.
segments.tr: - **経済活動。** 小売、レストラン、観光業界の団体は、外が明るいと消費者がより多く支出するとして、日照時間の延長を長年支持してきました。

segments.src: - **No more switching.** Ending the twice-yearly change removes the disruption it causes, including a short-term rise in some health and safety problems around the spring shift.
segments.tr: - **切り替えの廃止。** 年2回の変更をなくすことで、春の切り替え時期に発生する健康や安全上の問題の短期的増加など、それに伴う混乱を取り除くことができます。

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Standard Time
segments.tr: ## 恒久的な標準時を支持する論拠

segments.src: Many sleep scientists and medical groups favor the opposite approach.
segments.tr: 多くの睡眠科学者や医療団体は、逆のアプローチを支持しています。

segments.src: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine and other professional bodies have said that permanent standard time better matches the human body clock, because it aligns more closely with the natural cycle of sunrise and sunset.
segments.tr: 米国睡眠医学会（American Academy of Sleep Medicine）などの専門機関は、恒久的な標準時の方が、日の出と日没の自然なサイクルに近いため、人間の体内時計により適していると述べています。

segments.src: Their main points are:
segments.tr: 彼らの主な主張は以下の通りです。

segments.src: - **Circadian health.** Standard time puts more light in the morning, which helps regulate sleep and alertness. Permanent daylight time would mean very late sunrises in winter, especially in the western parts of time zones. In some places the sun would not rise until well after 8 a.m.
segments.tr: - **概日リズムの健康。** 標準時は朝の光を増やすため、睡眠と覚醒の調整に役立ちます。恒久的なサマータイムを採用すると、特にタイムゾーンの西部では冬の日の出が非常に遅くなります。場所によっては、午前8時を過ぎても日が昇らない地域も出てくるでしょう。

segments.src: - **Sleep and long-term health.** Researchers have linked chronic misalignment between social clocks and the body clock with sleep loss and other health problems. Advocates say standard time is the safer bet.
segments.tr: - **睡眠と長期的な健康。** 研究者は、社会的な時計と体内時計の慢性的な不一致が、睡眠不足やその他の健康問題に関連していると指摘しています。専門家は、標準時の方がより安全な選択であると主張しています。

segments.src: - **School mornings.** Children would commonly wait for buses and walk to school in the dark during winter months under permanent daylight time.
segments.tr: - **通学の朝。** 恒久的なサマータイムの下では、冬の間、子供たちは暗闇の中でバスを待ち、学校へ歩いて行くのが一般的になるでしょう。

segments.src: Evidence on both sides is real but imperfect.
segments.tr: 双方の証拠は本物ですが、完璧ではありません。

segments.src: Studies vary in method and in geography, and a benefit in one region can be a cost in another.
segments.tr: 研究によって手法や地理的条件は異なり、ある地域での利益が別の地域ではコストになることもあります。

segments.src: ## Lessons From the Past
segments.tr: ## 過去からの教訓

segments.src: The United States has tried this before.
segments.tr: 米国は以前にもこれを試みたことがあります。

segments.src: In 1974, Congress enacted year-round daylight time as a response to the energy crisis.
segments.tr: 1974年、議会はエネルギー危機への対応として、通年サマータイムを制定しました。

segments.src: Early public support faded within months as winter mornings stayed dark, and Congress reversed course the following year.
segments.tr: 冬の朝が暗いままだったため、国民の支持は数ヶ月で冷え込み、議会は翌年に方針を撤回しました。

segments.src: Supporters of permanence say today's circumstances are different.
segments.tr: 恒久化の支持者は、今日の状況は異なると言います。

segments.src: Critics say the episode is a warning.
segments.tr: 批判者は、このエピソードこそが警告であると述べています。

segments.src: ## Why Nothing Gets Done
segments.tr: ## なぜ何も進まないのか

segments.src: If both parties like the idea of ending clock changes, why is there no law?
segments.tr: もし両党とも時計の変更をやめるというアイデアを支持しているのなら、なぜ法律ができないのでしょうか？

segments.src: Several obstacles stand in the way.
segments.tr: いくつかの障害が立ちはだかっています。

segments.src: 1. **A split over which time.** Ending the switch is popular, but people who want permanent daylight time and people who want permanent standard time often oppose each other more than they oppose the status quo. A bill that satisfies one camp can lose the other.
segments.tr: 1. **どちらの時間にするかの分裂。** 切り替えをやめることは人気がありますが、恒久的なサマータイムを望む人々と、恒久的な標準時を望む人々は、現状維持を望む人々以上に互いに対立することがよくあります。一方の陣営を満足させる法案は、もう一方の陣営を失う可能性があります。

segments.src: 2. **Regional differences.** A sunrise at 8:30 a.m. is a minor matter in one part of a time zone and a serious one in another. Lawmakers from northern and western areas of a zone often have different priorities from those in the east.
segments.tr: 2. **地域差。** 午前8時30分の日の出は、タイムゾーンのある地域では些細な問題ですが、別の地域では深刻な問題です。タイムゾーンの北部や西部の議員は、東部の議員とは異なる優先順位を持っていることがよくあります。

segments.src: 3. **Competing priorities.** Time policy rarely ranks above budgets, security and health care on a crowded legislative calendar. Committee leaders may see it as a low-urgency item with high potential for backlash.
segments.tr: 3. **優先順位の競合。** 混雑した立法スケジュールにおいて、時間の政策が予算、安全保障、医療よりも優先されることはめったにありません。委員会のリーダーたちは、これを反発を招く可能性が高い、緊急性の低い案件と見なしている可能性があります。

segments.src: 4. **Industry and regional concerns.** Transportation, broadcasting, agriculture and finance all depend on time standards. Some businesses worry about misalignment with neighboring states or trading partners if states choose different paths.
segments.tr: 4. **産業および地域的な懸念。** 輸送、放送、農業、金融はすべて時間の基準に依存しています。一部の企業は、州が異なる道を選んだ場合、近隣の州や貿易相手国との不一致が生じることを懸念しています。

segments.src: 5. **Fear of repeating 1974.** Lawmakers remember that a popular change was reversed once voters felt the effects.
segments.tr: 5. **1974年の再来への恐怖。** 議員たちは、人気のある変更であっても、有権者がその影響を感じれば撤回されたという過去を記憶しています。

segments.src: ## The Statehouse Picture
segments.tr: ## 州議会の状況

segments.src: States keep acting even though they cannot finish the job.
segments.tr: 州は仕事を完遂できないと分かっていても、行動を続けています。

segments.src: Some legislatures have passed daylight-time trigger laws.
segments.tr: 一部の議会は、サマータイムへのトリガー法を可決しました。

segments.src: Others have considered bills for permanent standard time, which they are already allowed to adopt.
segments.tr: 他の議会では、すでに採用が認められている恒久的な標準時への法案を検討してきました。

segments.src: A few have proposed regional compacts so that neighboring states move together.
segments.tr: 近隣の州と足並みを揃えるために、地域協定を提案した州もいくつかあります。

segments.src: Each approach has trade-offs, and none solves the national question alone.
segments.tr: どのアプローチにもトレードオフがあり、どれ一つとして国家的な問題を単独で解決できるものはありません。

segments.src: ## What Could Break the Logjam
segments.tr: ## 行き詰まりを打開するには

segments.src: Possible paths include:
segments.tr: 考えられる道筋は以下の通りです。

segments.src: - **A compromise bill** that lets each state choose between permanent standard and permanent daylight time, with rules to limit confusion at borders.
segments.tr: - **妥協案としての法案。** 各州が恒久的な標準時か恒久的なサマータイムかを選択できるようにし、州境での混乱を制限するルールを設ける。

segments.src: - **A federal study** that gathers current evidence on health, safety and economic effects before Congress commits.
segments.tr: - **連邦政府による調査。** 議会が決定を下す前に、健康、安全、経済への影響に関する最新の証拠を収集する。

segments.src: - **Movement on standard time first**, since states can already adopt it without federal approval, which could build experience and data.
segments.tr: - **まずは標準時への移行。** 州は連邦の承認なしにすでに標準時を採用できるため、そこから経験とデータを蓄積する。

segments.src: Any of these would require sustained attention from leaders who have so far treated the issue as a seasonal curiosity.
segments.tr: これらを実行するには、これまでこの問題を季節ごとの好奇の対象として扱ってきたリーダーたちによる、継続的な関心が必要です。

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 結論

segments.src: The clock-change debate persists because it combines wide public frustration with a real scientific and political disagreement.
segments.tr: 時計の変更をめぐる議論が続くのは、それが広範な国民の不満と、科学的・政治的な真の意見の不一致を組み合わせているからです。

segments.src: Ending the switch is easy to endorse.
segments.tr: 切り替えをやめること自体は支持しやすいものです。

segments.src: Deciding which permanent time to choose, and who bears the cost of dark mornings or early sunsets, is much harder.
segments.tr: どちらの恒久的な時間を選択するか、そして暗い朝や早い日没のコストを誰が負担するかを決めることは、はるかに困難です。

segments.src: Until lawmakers settle that question, Americans can expect to keep adjusting their clocks twice a year, and to have this argument again each spring and fall.
segments.tr: 議員たちがその問題を解決するまで、アメリカ人は年に2回時計を調整し続け、春と秋が来るたびにこの議論を繰り返すことになるでしょう。

segments.tr: *この記事は一般的な情報提供を目的としており、医学的または法的な助言を構成するものではありません。*

segments.tr: Sie zeigte auch, wie wenig Konsens unter der Oberfläche lag.

segments.src: Several senators later said they had not examined the details, and some critics argued the chamber had acted without a serious look at the evidence.
segments.tr: Mehrere Senatoren erklärten später, sie hätten die Details nicht geprüft, und einige Kritiker argumentierten, die Kammer habe gehandelt, ohne die Beweise ernsthaft zu prüfen.

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Daylight Time
segments.tr: ## Die Argumente für die dauerhafte Sommerzeit

segments.src: Supporters of year-round daylight time point to several benefits:
segments.tr: Befürworter der ganzjährigen Sommerzeit verweisen auf mehrere Vorteile:

segments.src: - **Evening light.** Later sunsets year-round mean more daylight after work and school, which supporters say encourages outdoor activity, shopping and recreation.
segments.tr: - **Abendlicht.** Spätere Sonnenuntergänge das ganze Jahr über bedeuten mehr Tageslicht nach der Arbeit und der Schule, was nach Angaben der Befürworter Aktivitäten im Freien, Einkaufen und Erholung fördert.

segments.src: - **Safety.** Some studies suggest that more evening light can reduce certain crimes and may lower the risk of pedestrian crashes during the evening commute, when traffic is heavy.
segments.tr: - **Sicherheit.** Einige Studien legen nahe, dass mehr Abendlicht bestimmte Verbrechen reduzieren und das Risiko von Fußgängerunfällen während des abendlichen Berufsverkehrs, wenn der Verkehr stark ist, verringern kann.

segments.src: - **Economic activity.** Retail, restaurant and tourism groups have long backed extra daylight hours, arguing that consumers spend more when it is light out.
segments.tr: - **Wirtschaftliche Aktivität.** Einzelhandels-, Gastronomie- und Tourismusverbände unterstützen seit langem zusätzliche Stunden Tageslicht und argumentieren, dass Verbraucher mehr ausgeben, wenn es hell ist.

segments.src: - **No more switching.** Ending the twice-yearly change removes the disruption it causes, including a short-term rise in some health and safety problems around the spring shift.
segments.tr: - **Kein Umstellen mehr.** Die Abschaffung des zweimal jährlichen Wechsels beseitigt die damit verbundenen Störungen, einschließlich eines kurzfristigen Anstiegs einiger Gesundheits- und Sicherheitsprobleme rund um die Frühlingsumstellung.

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Standard Time
segments.tr: ## Die Argumente für die dauerhafte Normalzeit

segments.src: Many sleep scientists and medical groups favor the opposite approach.
segments.tr: Viele Schlafforscher und medizinische Vereinigungen bevorzugen den entgegengesetzten Ansatz.

segments.src: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine and other professional bodies have said that permanent standard time better matches the human body clock, because it aligns more closely with the natural cycle of sunrise and sunset.
segments.tr: Die American Academy of Sleep Medicine und andere Berufsverbände haben erklärt, dass die dauerhafte Normalzeit besser zur inneren Uhr des Menschen passt, da sie sich enger am natürlichen Zyklus von Sonnenaufgang und Sonnenuntergang ausrichtet.

segments.src: Their main points are:
segments.tr: Ihre Hauptpunkte sind:

segments.src: - **Circadian health.** Standard time puts more light in the morning, which helps regulate sleep and alertness. Permanent daylight time would mean very late sunrises in winter, especially in the western parts of time zones. In some places the sun would not rise until well after 8 a.m.
segments.tr: - **Zirkadiane Gesundheit.** Die Normalzeit bringt mehr Licht in den Morgen, was den Schlaf und die Wachsamkeit reguliert. Die dauerhafte Sommerzeit würde im Winter sehr späte Sonnenaufgänge bedeuten, insbesondere in den westlichen Teilen von Zeitzonen. An einigen Orten ging die Sonne erst weit nach 8 Uhr morgens auf.

segments.src: - **Sleep and long-term health.** Researchers have linked chronic misalignment between social clocks and the body clock with sleep loss and other health problems. Advocates say standard time is the safer bet.
segments.tr: - **Schlaf und langfristige Gesundheit.** Forscher haben eine chronische Fehlausrichtung zwischen sozialen Uhren und der inneren Uhr mit Schlafmangel und anderen gesundheitlichen Problemen in Verbindung gebracht. Befürworter sagen, die Normalzeit sei die sicherere Wahl.

segments.src: - **School mornings.** Children would commonly wait for buses and walk to school in the dark during winter months under permanent daylight time.
segments.tr: - **Schulmorgen.** Kinder würden in den Wintermonaten bei dauerhafter Sommerzeit häufig im Dunkeln auf Busse warten und zur Schule gehen.

segments.src: Evidence on both sides is real but imperfect.
segments.tr: Die Beweislage auf beiden Seiten ist real, aber unvollkommen.

segments.src: Studies vary in method and in geography, and a benefit in one region can be a cost in another.
segments.tr: Studien variieren in Methode und Geographie, und ein Vorteil in einer Region kann ein Nachteil in einer anderen sein.

segments.src: ## Lessons From the Past
segments.tr: ## Lehren aus der Vergangenheit

segments.src: The United States has tried this before.
segments.tr: Die Vereinigten Staaten haben dies bereits ausprobiert.

segments.src: In 1974, Congress enacted year-round daylight time as a response to the energy crisis.
segments.tr: 1974 beschloss der Kongress als Reaktion auf die Energiekrise die ganzjährige Sommerzeit.

segments.src: Early public support faded within months as winter mornings stayed dark, and Congress reversed course the following year.
segments.tr: Die anfängliche öffentliche Unterstützung schwand innerhalb weniger Monate, da die Wintermorgen dunkel blieben, und der Kongress machte den Kurs im folgenden Jahr rückgängig.

segments.src: Supporters of permanence say today's circumstances are different.
segments.tr: Befürworter der Dauerregelung sagen, die heutigen Umstände seien anders.

segments.src: Critics say the episode is a warning.
segments.tr: Kritiker sagen, die Episode sei eine Warnung.

segments.src: ## Why Nothing Gets Done
segments.tr: ## Warum nichts geschieht

segments.src: If both parties like the idea of ending clock changes, why is there no law?
segments.tr: Wenn beide Parteien die Idee der Abschaffung der Zeitumstellung gut finden, warum gibt es dann kein Gesetz?

segments.src: Several obstacles stand in the way.
segments.tr: Mehrere Hindernisse stehen im Weg.

segments.src: 1. **A split over which time.** Ending the switch is popular, but people who want permanent daylight time and people who want permanent standard time often oppose each other more than they oppose the status quo. A bill that satisfies one camp can lose the other.
segments.tr: 1. **Eine Spaltung darüber, welche Zeit.** Die Abschaffung des Wechsels ist beliebt, aber Menschen, die eine dauerhafte Sommerzeit wollen, und Menschen, die eine dauerhafte Normalzeit wollen, bekämpfen sich oft mehr als den Status quo. Ein Gesetzesentwurf, der ein Lager zufriedenstellt, kann das andere vergraulen.

segments.src: 2. **Regional differences.** A sunrise at 8:30 a.m. is a minor matter in one part of a time zone and a serious one in another. Lawmakers from northern and western areas of a zone often have different priorities from those in the east.
segments.tr: 2. **Regionale Unterschiede.** Ein Sonnenaufgang um 8:30 Uhr ist in einem Teil einer Zeitzone eine Kleinigkeit und in einem anderen eine ernsthafte Angelegenheit. Gesetzgeber aus nördlichen und westlichen Regionen einer Zone haben oft andere Prioritäten als die im Osten.

segments.src: 3. **Competing priorities.** Time policy rarely ranks above budgets, security and health care on a crowded legislative calendar. Committee leaders may see it as a low-urgency item with high potential for backlash.
segments.tr: 3. **Konkurrierende Prioritäten.** Die Zeitpolitik rangiert in einem überfüllten Gesetzgebungskalender selten vor Budgets, Sicherheit und Gesundheitsversorgung. Ausschussvorsitzende betrachten sie möglicherweise als Punkt mit geringer Dringlichkeit und hohem Rückschlagpotenzial.

segments.src: 4. **Industry and regional concerns.** Transportation, broadcasting, agriculture and finance all depend on time standards. Some businesses worry about misalignment with neighboring states or trading partners if states choose different paths.
segments.tr: 4. **Industrie- und regionale Bedenken.** Transport, Rundfunk, Landwirtschaft und Finanzwesen hängen alle von Zeitstandards ab. Einige Unternehmen machen sich Sorgen über eine Fehlausrichtung mit benachbarten Bundesstaaten oder Handelspartnern, wenn Bundesstaaten unterschiedliche Wege wählen.

segments.src: 5. **Fear of repeating 1974.** Lawmakers remember that a popular change was reversed once voters felt the effects.
segments.tr: 5. **Angst vor einer Wiederholung von 1974.** Die Gesetzgeber erinnern sich daran, dass eine populäre Änderung rückgängig gemacht wurde, sobald die Wähler die Auswirkungen spürten.

segments.src: ## The Statehouse Picture
segments.tr: ## Das Bild in den Parlamenten der Bundesstaaten

segments.src: States keep acting even though they cannot finish the job.
segments.tr: Die Bundesstaaten handeln weiter, obwohl sie die Arbeit nicht zu Ende führen können.

segments.src: Some legislatures have passed daylight-time trigger laws.
segments.tr: Einige Parlamente haben Gesetze zur Auslösung der Sommerzeit verabschiedet.

segments.src: Others have considered bills for permanent standard time, which they are already allowed to adopt.
segments.tr: Andere haben Gesetzesentwürfe für eine dauerhafte Normalzeit geprüft, deren Einführung ihnen bereits erlaubt ist.

segments.src: A few have proposed regional compacts so that neighboring states move together.
segments.tr: Einige wenige haben regionale Abkommen vorgeschlagen, damit benachbarte Bundesstaaten gemeinsam vorgehen.

segments.src: Each approach has trade-offs, and none solves the national question alone.
segments.tr: Jeder Ansatz hat Kompromisse, und keiner löst die nationale Frage allein.

segments.src: ## What Could Break the Logjam
segments.tr: ## Was den Stillstand beheben könnte

segments.src: Possible paths include:
segments.tr: Mögliche Wege umfassen:

segments.src: - **A compromise bill** that lets each state choose between permanent standard and permanent daylight time, with rules to limit confusion at borders.
segments.tr: - **Ein Kompromissgesetz**, das jedem Bundesstaat die Wahl zwischen dauerhafter Normal- und dauerhafter Sommerzeit lässt, mit Regeln zur Begrenzung von Verwirrung an den Grenzen.

segments.src: - **A federal study** that gathers current evidence on health, safety and economic effects before Congress commits.
segments.tr: - **Eine bundesweite Studie**, die aktuelle Beweise zu gesundheitlichen, sicherheitsbezogenen und wirtschaftlichen Auswirkungen sammelt, bevor sich der Kongress festlegt.

segments.src: - **Movement on standard time first**, since states can already adopt it without federal approval, which could build experience and data.
segments.tr: - **Zuerst Fortschritte bei der Normalzeit**, da Bundesstaaten diese bereits ohne bundesstaatliche Genehmigung annehmen können, was Erfahrung und Daten aufbauen könnte.

segments.src: Any of these would require sustained attention from leaders who have so far treated the issue as a seasonal curiosity.
segments.tr: Jeder dieser Schritte würde anhaltende Aufmerksamkeit von Führungspersönlichkeiten erfordern, die das Thema bisher als saisonale Kuriosität behandelt haben.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Das Fazit

segments.src: The clock-change debate persists because it combines wide public frustration with a real scientific and political disagreement.
segments.tr: Die Debatte über die Zeitumstellung hält an, da sie breite öffentliche Frustration mit einer echten wissenschaftlichen und politischen Uneinigkeit verbindet.

segments.src: Ending the switch is easy to endorse.
segments.tr: Die Abschaffung des Wechsels ist leicht zu befürworten.

segments.src: Deciding which permanent time to choose, and who bears the cost of dark mornings or early sunsets, is much harder.
segments.tr: Zu entscheiden, welche dauerhafte Zeit gewählt werden soll und wer die Kosten für dunkle Morgen oder frühe Sonnenuntergänge trägt, ist viel schwieriger.

segments.src: Until lawmakers settle that question, Americans can expect to keep adjusting their clocks twice a year, and to have this argument again each spring and fall.
segments.tr: Bis die Gesetzgeber diese Frage klären, können die Amerikaner erwarten, dass sie ihre Uhren weiterhin zweimal im Jahr umstellen und diesen Streit jeden Früh- und Herbst wieder austragen müssen.

vi.title: Quay Trở Lại: Tại Sao Cuộc Tranh Cãi Về Giờ Tiết Kiệm Ánh Sáng Ban Ngày Vĩnh Viễn Vẫn Không Đi Đến Đâu

segments.src: Every autumn, Americans gain an hour of sleep and lose an hour of evening light.
segments.tr: Mỗi mùa thu, người Mỹ có thêm một giờ ngủ và mất đi một giờ ánh sáng buổi chiều.

segments.src: With clocks having just turned back for the year, a familiar question returns: why are we still doing this twice a year?
segments.tr: Khi đồng hồ vừa quay ngược lại trong năm, một câu hỏi quen thuộc lại xuất hiện: tại sao chúng ta vẫn làm điều này hai lần một năm?

segments.src: Polls regularly show that many Americans would like to stop changing the clocks.
segments.tr: Các cuộc thăm dò thường xuyên cho thấy nhiều người Mỹ muốn dừng việc thay đổi đồng hồ.

segments.src: Yet years of bills, hearings and statehouse debates have produced no national change.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, nhiều năm dự án luật, phiên điều trần và tranh luận tại các cơ quan lập pháp bang đã không mang lại thay đổi nào ở cấp quốc gia.

segments.src: The reason has less to do with indifference than with a disagreement over which time to keep.
segments.tr: Lý do ít liên quan đến sự thờ ơ mà liên quan nhiều hơn đến sự bất đồng về việc nên giữ múi giờ nào.

segments.src: ## Where the Law Stands
segments.tr: ## Tình Trạng Pháp Lý Hiện Tại

segments.src: Under the Uniform Time Act of 1966, states may opt out of daylight saving time and stay on standard time all year.
segments.tr: Theo Đạo luật Giờ Thống nhất năm 1966, các bang có quyền không tham gia giờ tiết kiệm ánh sáng ban ngày và duy trì giờ chuẩn quanh năm.

segments.src: Arizona (apart from the Navajo Nation) and Hawaii have done so.
segments.tr: Arizona (trừ Vùng đất của người Navajo) và Hawaii đã làm như vậy.

segments.src: States cannot, however, adopt permanent daylight saving time on their own.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, các bang không thể tự ý áp dụng giờ tiết kiệm ánh sáng ban ngày vĩnh viễn.

segments.src: That change requires an act of Congress.
segments.tr: Sự thay đổi đó đòi hỏi phải có đạo luật của Quốc hội.

segments.src: Dozens of states have passed laws or resolutions that would move to year-round daylight time if Congress allowed it.
segments.tr: Hàng chục bang đã thông qua các luật hoặc nghị quyết chuyển sang giờ ban ngày quanh năm nếu Quốc hội cho phép.

segments.src: These measures are often called "trigger" laws because they take effect only after federal permission.
segments.tr: Các biện pháp này thường được gọi là luật "kích hoạt" vì chúng chỉ có hiệu lực sau khi có sự cho phép của liên bang.

segments.src: This leaves a patchwork of intentions with no clear path forward.
segments.tr: Điều này tạo ra một bức tranh chắp vá về các ý định mà không có hướng đi rõ ràng.

segments.src: ## The Bill That Almost Was
segments.tr: ## Dự Luật Suýt Thành Hiện Thực

segments.src: The best-known attempt was the Sunshine Protection Act.
segments.tr: Nỗ lực nổi tiếng nhất là Đạo luật Bảo vệ Ánh nắng.

segments.src: In March 2022 the Senate passed it by unanimous consent, with little debate.
segments.tr: Vào tháng 3 năm 2022, Thượng viện đã thông qua đạo luật này bằng sự đồng thuận tuyệt đối, với rất ít tranh luận.

segments.src: The bill would have made daylight saving time permanent nationwide.
segments.tr: Dự luật này sẽ làm cho giờ tiết kiệm ánh sáng ban ngày trở thành vĩnh viễn trên toàn quốc.

segments.src: The House did not take it up, and the bill expired at the end of that session.
segments.tr: Hạ viện đã không đưa ra xem xét, và dự luật đã hết hiệu lực vào cuối kỳ họp đó.

segments.src: Versions have been reintroduced in later Congresses with bipartisan sponsors, and they have again stalled in committee.
segments.tr: Các phiên bản khác đã được giới thiệu lại trong các Quốc hội sau với các nhà tài trợ từ cả hai đảng, và chúng lại tiếp tục bị đình trệ tại ủy ban.

segments.src: The 2022 episode is often cited as proof of how popular the idea is.
segments.tr: Sự kiện năm 2022 thường được dẫn chứng làm bằng chứng cho thấy ý tưởng này được ủng hộ rộng rãi đến mức nào.

segments.src: It also showed how little consensus lay beneath the surface.
segments.tr: Nó cũng cho thấy có rất ít sự đồng thuận ẩn chứa bên dưới bề mặt.

segments.src: Several senators later said they had not examined the details, and some critics argued the chamber had acted without a serious look at the evidence.
segments.tr: Một số thượng nghị sĩ sau đó cho biết họ chưa xem xét kỹ các chi tiết, và một số nhà phê bình lập luận rằng viện này đã hành động mà không xem xét nghiêm túc các bằng chứng.

segments.src: ## The Case for Permanent Daylight Time
segments.tr: ## Lập Luận Cho Giờ Ban Ngày Vĩnh Viễn

segments.tr: Những người ủng hộ giờ ban ngày quanh năm chỉ ra một số lợi ích:

segments.tr: - **Ánh sáng buổi chiều.** Hoàng hôn muộn hơn quanh năm có nghĩa là có nhiều ánh sáng ban ngày hơn sau giờ làm việc và học tập, mà những người ủng hộ cho biết sẽ khuyến khích các hoạt động ngoài trời, mua sắm và giải trí.

segments.src: - **Safety.** Some studies suggest that more evening light can reduce certain crimes and may lower the risk of pedestrian crashes during the evening commute, when traffic is heavy.
segments.tr: - **An toàn.** Một số nghiên cứu cho rằng nhiều ánh sáng buổi chiều hơn có thể làm giảm một số tội phạm và có thể làm giảm nguy cơ tai nạn cho người đi bộ trong giờ cao điểm buổi chiều, khi giao thông đông đúc.

segments.src: - **Economic activity.** Retail, restaurant and tourism groups have long backed extra daylight hours, arguing that consumers spend more when it is light out.
segments.tr: - **Hoạt động kinh tế.** Các nhóm bán lẻ, nhà hàng và du lịch từ lâu đã ủng hộ việc có thêm giờ ban ngày, với lập luận rằng người tiêu dùng chi tiêu nhiều hơn khi trời còn sáng.

segments.src: - **No more switching.** Ending the twice-yearly change removes the disruption it causes, including a short-term rise in some health and safety problems around the spring shift.
segments.tr: - **Không còn đổi giờ nữa.** Việc chấm dứt sự thay đổi hai lần một năm sẽ loại bỏ sự gián đoạn do nó gây ra, bao gồm sự gia tăng ngắn hạn về một số vấn đề sức khỏe và an toàn quanh thời điểm chuyển đổi mùa xuân.

segments.tr: ## Lập Luận Cho Giờ Chuẩn Vĩnh Viễn

segments.tr: - **Sức khỏe nhịp sinh học.** Giờ chuẩn mang lại nhiều ánh sáng hơn vào buổi sáng, giúp điều hòa giấc ngủ và sự tỉnh táo. Giờ tiết kiệm ánh sáng ban ngày vĩnh viễn sẽ có nghĩa là mặt trời mọc rất muộn vào mùa đông, đặc biệt là ở các khu vực phía tây của các múi giờ. Ở một số nơi, mặt trời sẽ không mọc cho đến tận sau 8 giờ sáng.

segments.src: Evidence on both sides is real but imperfect.
segments.tr: Bằng chứng từ cả hai phía là có thật nhưng chưa hoàn hảo.

segments.tr: Các nghiên cứu khác nhau về phương pháp và địa lý, và một lợi ích ở khu vực này có thể là một tổn thất ở khu vực khác.

segments.src: ## Lessons From the Past
segments.tr: ## Bài Học Từ Quá Khứ

segments.src: The United States has tried this before.
segments.tr: Hoa Kỳ đã từng thử điều này trước đây.

segments.src: In 1974, Congress enacted year-round daylight time as a response to the energy crisis.
segments.tr: Vào năm 1974, Quốc hội đã ban hành giờ ban ngày quanh năm như một phản ứng đối với cuộc khủng hoảng năng lượng.

segments.src: Early public support faded within months as winter mornings stayed dark, and Congress reversed course the following year.
segments.tr: Sự ủng hộ ban đầu của công chúng đã phai nhạt trong vòng vài tháng khi buổi sáng mùa đông vẫn tối, và Quốc hội đã đảo ngược quyết định vào năm sau.

segments.src: Supporters of permanence say today's circumstances are different.
segments.tr: Những người ủng hộ việc giữ nguyên vĩnh viễn cho biết hoàn cảnh ngày nay đã khác.

segments.src: Critics say the episode is a warning.
segments.tr: Các nhà phê bình cho rằng sự việc đó là một lời cảnh báo.

segments.src: ## Why Nothing Gets Done
segments.tr: ## Tại Sao Không Có Gì Được Hoàn Thành

segments.src: If both parties like the idea of ending clock changes, why is there no law?
segments.tr: Nếu cả hai đảng đều thích ý tưởng chấm dứt việc thay đổi đồng hồ, tại sao lại không có luật nào được thông qua?

segments.src: Several obstacles stand in the way.
segments.tr: Một số trở ngại đang ngáng đường.

segments.src: 1. **A split over which time.** Ending the switch is popular, but people who want permanent daylight time and people who want permanent standard time often oppose each other more than they oppose the status quo. A bill that satisfies one camp can lose the other.
segments.tr: 1. **Sự chia rẽ về việc chọn giờ nào.** Chấm dứt việc chuyển đổi rất phổ biến, nhưng những người muốn giờ ban ngày vĩnh viễn và những người muốn giờ chuẩn vĩnh viễn thường chống đối lẫn nhau nhiều hơn là chống đối hiện trạng. Một dự luật làm hài lòng phe này có thể làm mất lòng phe kia.

segments.src: 2. **Regional differences.** A sunrise at 8:30 a.m. is a minor matter in one part of a time zone and a serious one in another. Lawmakers from northern and western areas of a zone often have different priorities from those in the east.
segments.tr: 2. **Sự khác biệt vùng miền.** Mặt trời mọc lúc 8:30 sáng là một vấn đề nhỏ ở phần này của múi giờ nhưng lại là vấn đề nghiêm trọng ở phần khác. Các nhà lập pháp từ các khu vực phía bắc và phía tây của một múi giờ thường có các ưu tiên khác với những người ở phía đông.

segments.src: 3. **Competing priorities.** Time policy rarely ranks above budgets, security and health care on a crowded legislative calendar. Committee leaders may see it as a low-urgency item with high potential for backlash.
segments.tr: 3. **Các ưu tiên cạnh tranh.** Chính sách thời gian hiếm khi xếp trên ngân sách, an ninh và chăm sóc sức khỏe trong một lịch trình lập pháp đông đúc. Các nhà lãnh đạo ủy ban có thể coi đây là một vấn đề ít khẩn cấp với tiềm năng gây phản ứng dữ dội cao.

segments.src: 4. **Industry and regional concerns.** Transportation, broadcasting, agriculture and finance all depend on time standards. Some businesses worry about misalignment with neighboring states or trading partners if states choose different paths.
segments.tr: 4. **Mối quan tâm của ngành và vùng miền.** Giao thông vận tải, phát thanh truyền hình, nông nghiệp và tài chính đều phụ thuộc vào tiêu chuẩn thời gian. Một số doanh nghiệp lo ngại về sự sai lệch với các bang láng giềng hoặc đối tác thương mại nếu các bang chọn những con đường khác nhau.

segments.src: 5. **Fear of repeating 1974.** Lawmakers remember that a popular change was reversed once voters felt the effects.
segments.tr: 5. **Nỗi sợ lặp lại năm 1974.** Các nhà lập pháp nhớ rằng một sự thay đổi phổ biến đã bị đảo ngược ngay khi cử tri cảm nhận được tác động.

segments.src: ## The Statehouse Picture
segments.tr: ## Bức Tranh Cơ Quan Lập Pháp Các Bang

segments.src: States keep acting even though they cannot finish the job.
segments.tr: Các bang vẫn tiếp tục hành động mặc dù họ không thể hoàn thành công việc.

segments.src: Some legislatures have passed daylight-time trigger laws.
segments.tr: Một số cơ quan lập pháp đã thông qua luật kích hoạt giờ ban ngày.

segments.src: Others have considered bills for permanent standard time, which they are already allowed to adopt.
segments.tr: Những nơi khác đã xem xét các dự luật về giờ chuẩn vĩnh viễn, thứ mà họ đã được phép áp dụng.

segments.src: A few have proposed regional compacts so that neighboring states move together.
segments.tr: Một số ít đã đề xuất các hiệp ước khu vực để các bang láng giềng cùng di chuyển.

segments.src: Each approach has trade-offs, and none solves the national question alone.
segments.tr: Mỗi cách tiếp cận đều có sự đánh đổi, và không có cách nào tự giải quyết được câu hỏi quốc gia.

segments.src: ## What Could Break the Logjam
segments.tr: ## Điều Gì Có Thể Phá Vỡ Thế Bế Tắc

segments.src: Possible paths include:
segments.tr: Các con đường khả thi bao gồm:

segments.src: - **A compromise bill** that lets each state choose between permanent standard and permanent daylight time, with rules to limit confusion at borders.
segments.tr: - **Một dự luật thỏa hiệp** cho phép mỗi bang lựa chọn giữa giờ chuẩn vĩnh viễn và giờ ban ngày vĩnh viễn, kèm theo các quy tắc để hạn chế sự nhầm lẫn ở biên giới.

segments.src: - **A federal study** that gathers current evidence on health, safety and economic effects before Congress commits.
segments.tr: - **Một nghiên cứu liên bang** thu thập bằng chứng hiện tại về tác động sức khỏe, an toàn và kinh tế trước khi Quốc hội cam kết.

segments.src: - **Movement on standard time first**, since states can already adopt it without federal approval, which could build experience and data.
segments.tr: - **Hành động về giờ chuẩn trước**, vì các bang đã có thể áp dụng nó mà không cần sự chấp thuận của liên bang, điều này có thể xây dựng kinh nghiệm và dữ liệu.

segments.src: Any of these would require sustained attention from leaders who have so far treated the issue as a seasonal curiosity.
segments.tr: Bất kỳ điều nào trong số này cũng đòi hỏi sự chú ý liên tục từ các nhà lãnh đạo, những người cho đến nay vẫn coi vấn đề này như một sự tò mò theo mùa.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Điểm Mấu Chốt

segments.src: The clock-change debate persists because it combines wide public frustration with a real scientific and political disagreement.
segments.tr: Tranh cãi về việc thay đổi đồng hồ vẫn tồn tại vì nó kết hợp sự thất vọng rộng rãi của công chúng với một sự bất đồng khoa học và chính trị thực sự.

segments.src: Ending the switch is easy to endorse.
segments.tr: Chấm dứt việc chuyển đổi là điều dễ dàng để ủng hộ.

segments.src: Deciding which permanent time to choose, and who bears the cost of dark mornings or early sunsets, is much harder.
segments.tr: Quyết định nên chọn giờ vĩnh viễn nào, và ai gánh chịu chi phí của buổi sáng tối trời hay hoàng hôn sớm, lại khó khăn hơn nhiều.

segments.src: Until lawmakers settle that question, Americans can expect to keep adjusting their clocks twice a year, and to have this argument again each spring and fall.
segments.tr: Cho đến khi các nhà lập pháp giải quyết xong câu hỏi đó, người Mỹ có thể mong đợi tiếp tục điều chỉnh đồng hồ của họ hai lần một năm, và lại tranh cãi về điều này vào mỗi mùa xuân và mùa thu.
